candidates.similarity: Noah's family is at issue in the flood survival narrative.
candidates.difference: Genesis includes Noah's sons among ark survivors; Qur'an 11:42–46 narrates a son refusing rescue and explicitly rejects biological kinship as sufficient.

candidates.similarity: Noah and his household emerge after the flood under divine instruction and blessing.
candidates.difference: Genesis narrates altar, sacrifice, divine covenant and rainbow; Qur'an 11:48 speaks of peace, blessings and later communities including those facing punishment.

research_dossier.title: Noah after the Flood: kinship, disembarkation, blessing and covenant
research_dossier.chronology_note: Genesis is an ancient Israelite textual tradition preserved in later manuscript witnesses; precise literary strata and date of composition remain debated. Do not conflate composition, redaction, translation and surviving manuscript dates.
research_dossier.comparison_note: Keep the contradiction in family outcomes explicit, and distinguish post-flood blessing from the Genesis covenant narrative. No claim of direct Qur'anic dependence follows from episode similarity.
